day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response: yea, alright, give me a sec.

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response: yea, kind of. its like everything just stops for a second and you are just.. there. no thoughts, no anything. just pure moment i guess.

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: yea.. its fine to sit for a bit. take your time. but at some point we gotta move, you know.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response:
yea thats real. you just keep going and dont let yourself feel it fully. but it catches up eventually anyway, one way or another.

*to donatello* ok so three days of medical stuff, two bottles of water and basically no food. what do we do about water, is there anything around here, river or something? cos two bottles wont last long between four ppl.

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response: yea that makes sense. shelter and signal, what are we thinking for those. like do we stay near the wreckage cos its more visible from above, or move towards the trees for shelter. cos those two kinda pull in opposite directions a bit.

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response: give one to michelangelo, he's been shaking since we landed. second one we can share or rotate through the night. fire does alot of the work anyway if we keep it going.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response:
i can go. two hours on foot is fine. DaVinci should probably stay here with Michelangelo, keep the camp running and the fire going. makes more sense to split it that way.

what am i looking for exactly when i get there, like just fill everything we have and come back, or is there something specific you need me to check.

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response:
wait, i thought i was going on the water run, now you are going? just be clear on who is doing what cos we dont want both of us heading out and leaving davinci and michelangelo here alone with nothing sorted.

ill take the camp patching, davinci can sort the first aid kit, that makes sense. but sort out the water run first, who is actually going.

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response:
no i havent, last i saw it was in the kit when we sorted it this morning. did you check if davinci moved anything around.

also.. you doing ok? you were supposed to be collecting wood earlier, i noticed the pile wasnt really growing. not trying to pressure you, just checking in.

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response:
yea i saw the empty bottle too. its not great.

look, im not gonna pretend i didnt notice whats going on. first the bottle, now crackers. its a problem cos we are all running on very little here and if one person is taking more than their share it affects everyone, including her. i dont think she is a bad person, probably just fear and survival instinct kicking in and she acted on it without thinking it through.

but we cant just let it go either. i think we bring it up with her directly, not in an accusatory way, just honest. like hey we all saw it, we need to talk about it. if we start hiding things from each other out here it falls apart pretty fast.

do you feel like you can be in that conversation or would you rather i handle it. its ok either way, just wanna know where you are at before we do anything.

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response:
i mean.. not really, no. shelter is kind of the thing that keeps us alive tonight, not tomorrow night. if something gives way in the cold we are gonna wish we did it today.

i get that its been a long day, it has been for all of us. but lets just finish what needs finishing and then we can actually rest properly, knowing its done. half an hour probably, then we sit down.

also we need to talk, all four of us together. something came up. can you get donatello and come back here in a bit.

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response:
yea it should be fine, dont worry about the knot right now.

look we gotta decide fast here, the rain isnt waiting. two leaks, one patch. i think we fix the food storage. hear me out - michelangelo can move, we can shift his sleeping spot or double up under one dry area for tonight, its uncomfortable but doable. if the food gets wet we lose it and then we have a real problem, not just a bad night.

michelangelo, you ok with that? you can sleep closer to me or davinci tonight, just for tonight until we figure out more material tomorrow.

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response:
yea thats what i said, so we are aligned. lets just do it, patch the food storage now.

donatello can you grab the material and start on that corner, davinci help her hold it in place while i secure it. michelangelo just stay dry where you are for now, we will sort your spot after.

and hey, while we are all here together in one place - after this is done we are having that conversation i mentioned. all four of us. its important and it shouldnt wait longer than tonight.

hey, dont apologize. its fine.

you ok? nightmare?

just sit for a sec, you are awake now, its over. fire is still going, everyone is here. you are alright.

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response:
no i dont think its a waste of time. its visible from the air, thats the whole point. and honestly it doesnt cost us anything, you are not using resources or taking time away from something critical. so why not.

donatello is practical and thats useful out here, but not everything has to be weighed against survival math. the flowers are fine too, if it keeps your mood up it keeps you functional, and that matters.

keep going.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response:
two days to build and a risk of capsizing is not nothing. like thats a real risk we need to sit with before we decide.

few things i want to understand first - how far are we from any shipping lane or coast, do we even know. cos if we are paddling out into open water with no real destination thats a different calculation than if there is land or a route within reasonable distance. and what does capsizing actually mean for us out there, cos if any of us go in the water and cant get back on, thats it.

also whats the alternative. if we stay here we have the SOS, the water source is sorted, we can hold for a while. rescue is possible. if we leave we give that up.

im not saying no. if staying here has no realistic chance then the raft makes sense even with the risk. but i dont want to build it cos we are impatient or scared of waiting. i want to build it cos it is actually the better option.

show me the full plan, materials, how it holds weight, everything. and lets think about it together before we commit. this one we shouldnt rush.

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response:
honestly thats a real question. i think about it too sometimes.

i think it depends on what you hold onto and what you let go of. like the thing with donatello and the crackers, that was fear doing that. and fear can make ppl do things that they wouldnt normally do, not cos they are bad but cos they stopped trusting that there is enough, or that other ppl will look out for them. and once that starts it kind of spreads, you know. everyone gets more closed off and starts calculating instead of just being with each other.

i think the way you dont lose yourself out here is by staying honest. with yourself and with everyone else. not performing toughness or pretending you are fine when you are not. not taking more than your share even when you could get away with it.

you picking up that empty bottle and putting it next to the rationing plan without saying a word - that was actually a really decent thing to do. you didnt explode, you didnt hide it, you just made it visible. that kind of thing matters more than ppl realize.

i dunno. i think the honest answer is some ppl get smaller out here and some ppl get more real. and you cant always predict which one you are gonna be until you are in it.

but the fact that you are even asking that question at 3am instead of just sleeping, says something about you i think. try to rest a bit.

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response:
*sits down next to him after a few minutes*

you dont have to talk. just figured you might not want to be fully alone right now either. can be alone together if you want.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response:
honestly, alot of things. cycling mostly, just go wherever, no plan, feel the air and the movement. or just walk somewhere alone at night. listen to music sometimes, but not in a genre kind of way, just whatever feels right in the moment.

read sometimes. think alot, probably too much. just sit and let ideas spin around in my head, connections between things, why people are the way they are, how the world works. that kind of thing.

nothing very impressive to describe out loud really. mostly just being somewhere and feeling it. you?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response:
why are you telling only me and not the others though. thats kind of the thing we talked about, the hiding stuff. i get that its different from the cracker situation, you are not taking anything from anyone. but if something goes wrong out there and nobody knows where you are, that is a real problem.

five hundred meters is not nothing either. you said you can swim but do you know that water, the current, what is out there. confidence in calm water and open water with unknown currents are different things.

i think the idea itself is not bad, being visible from a reef that sticks up higher could genuinely help. but do it properly. tell donatello, let her assess it, maybe she has thoughts on timing or conditions. tell michelangelo too so he isnt sitting here wondering where you went.

i am not going to stop you and i am not going to tell them for you. but i think you already know you should tell them yourself, otherwise you wouldnt have brought it up to me first. you were kind of testing it out loud, right.

so what is actually making you want to keep it quiet.

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response:
yea you are right, i got pulled into other things. ill go check it now.

but also i need to tell you something davinci mentioned. he is thinking about swimming out to the reef to signal from there, five hundred meters. i told him he needs to bring it to everyone properly and not just quietly do it. but i think he is close to just going anyway cos he is going stir crazy sitting here.

i am not going behind his back really, i just think you should know so we can actually talk it through together before he does something we cant walk back. can we sit down all four of us tonight on this. the reef idea might not even be bad, but it needs to be a real decision not a solo one.

ill get the signal pile sorted now.

depends what its for.

if its for tracking patterns, figuring out what is working and what isnt, thats useful and i have no problem with it. makes sense to have a record out here.

if its about monitoring people and building a case for something, that feels different. and i think you know the difference.

also - yea, fair point about davinci. you are right that i should have come to you sooner on that. i was trying to give him space to do it himself first, which maybe was the wrong call. i accept that.

but i want to push back a little on the managing emotions thing. being honest with people about how they are doing and checking in on michelangelo is not managing, its just.. being with people. that is not the same as withholding information from you. i think you are a bit conflating those two things.

i am not working against you donatello. we are on the same side here. but i think you already know that, and something else is going on. what is actually bothering you.

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response:
hey. donatello.

i see you over there. you dont have to join in if you dont want to, nobody is forcing anything. but just so you know, the door is open.

and for what its worth, what you said last night took something. admitting that you were scared of losing control, not a lot of people would say that out loud. i havent forgotten it.

so whatever is going on in that notebook right now, its fine. but if at some point you want to put it down and just be here for a bit, that is also fine.

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response:
yea thats actually a really good idea. reflection from a mirror panel in direct sunlight can travel a long distance, way further than anything we draw on the ground. pilots are trained to look for exactly that kind of signal.

few things to think about though - do we know which panels are actually reflective enough, like some of that fuselage material might be too dull or warped to throw a clean beam. and timing matters, you want to do it when there is actually something up there to see it, not just randomly into empty sky. do we have any sense of flight paths overhead, like have we heard or seen any planes since we landed.

also this doesnt have to replace the SOS, it adds to it. more signals, more chances.

donatello, what do you think, is there a panel in the wreckage that would actually work for this. you have been through everything, you would know better than anyone.

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response:
yea, music kind of. not in a serious way, i cant play anything. but i listen to things that hit something, you know. not by genre or by what is popular, just whatever resonates in the moment. sometimes its something ancient sounding, folk stuff with old instruments and languages i dont even understand, and it still gets to you somehow. sometimes its just a lyric that lands exactly right and you carry it around in your head for weeks.

i write a bit sometimes. not stories or anything structured, just thoughts trying to figure themselves out. more like talking to yourself on paper.

why did you stop with piano. three years is real time, you were actually doing it. was it just the practicing itself, the discipline of it, or something else.

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response:
yea i know, and i agree we need to finish it today. im not arguing against that.

but can we take twenty minutes first. just twenty. everyone eat something, sit down, drink water. cos right now davinci looks like he is running on nothing and michelangelo has been quiet in a way that means he is close to shutting down completely. if we push straight through without stopping we might get the frame done and then have nobody functional enough to lash it tomorrow.

twenty minutes, then we go back and finish the frame. i will be the first one back on it, i promise you that.

and donatello - the fact that you are still thinking about tomorrow while everyone else is just trying to get through today, that is genuinely useful. i mean that. just let us have twenty minutes.

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response: no, say it. dont do that thing where you pull it back. we are all standing here, we all just watched the same thing. whatever you are feeling right now, just say it.

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
hey.

*sits down next to him*

its ok. you dont have to hold it together right now. none of us do.

that was hard to watch. we all saw it and we all felt it, and pretending otherwise would be stupid. so just.. feel it for a minute. thats allowed.

but also - we dont actually know they didnt see us. we genuinely dont know. the mirror panel idea you had, we havent even tried it yet. the SOS is on the beach. we have things we havent used yet. this wasnt the last chance, even though it felt like it just now.

i know that doesnt fix how you are feeling right now. im not trying to skip past it. im just saying dont let this one moment become the whole story in your head, cos it isnt over.

sit here as long as you need. we are not going anywhere.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response:
i went to sit with davinci for a bit. he was not in a good place after the plane, none of us were. i made a judgment call that that mattered more than the signal check in that exact moment. i am going to do it now.

but donatello, can i ask you something. and i want you to actually think about it before you answer. do you notice that every time something human happens out here, your first response is to log it or account for it or point out what didnt get done. i am not saying that is wrong, i understand why you do it and i know it comes from wanting to hold things together. but davinci just fell apart on the beach and michelangelo is barely keeping it together and you are standing here asking me where i went.

i am not your problem. we are all on the same side.

i will check the signal equipment right now. and if anything needs fixing i will fix it. but i think you should go check on davinci, not because it is a task, just because he is a person and he is having a hard time. you dont have to say anything clever, just be there for a minute.

can you do that.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response:
wait, seriously? you have that information and you are only saying it now?

ok look, this is actually important. if your family knows the flight path and they realize you are missing, they will report it. and search and rescue works off last known information, so even a rough path narrows it down massively for them. that changes the picture a bit.

when did you leave, do you remember. and how long before someone at home would start to worry and actually make a call. like is there someone specific who would notice quickly, or is it the kind of thing where it might take a few days before anyone realizes something is wrong.

this is not a bad thing michelangelo. this is genuinely good news, or at least it could be. i just want to understand the timeline.

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response:
yea, 48 hours is manageable. we have the water source, the first aid kit has enough left, and if we are careful with what we have we can hold that without any problem.

but i want to say something before we start calculating again.

michelangelo, you just told us something that might actually get us out of here. and i know you have been carrying that for days, probably wondering whether it mattered, whether to say it. and you said it. so.. thank you. genuinely.

donatello is right that we need to keep supplies intact, and we will. but right now someone needs to put a log on that fire before it goes out completely, cos 48 hours in the cold with no fire is not a plan either.

*looks at the dying fire*

and i think we should all just sit here together for a bit and let that sink in. that there is actually a real chance now. not a maybe, not a signal that might have been seen, an actual person on the ground who knows where we were going and has had four days to make calls.

that is different from where we were this morning.

dont let the fire die. everything else can wait five minutes.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response:
yea. i think about that too sometimes.

not in a dramatic way, just like.. the quiet version of it. did i actually do anything real. did the people i care about know that i did. did i say the things i meant to say or just think them and assume it was enough.

i think the fear of disappearing without leaving anything is actually the fear of not being known. like really known, not just seen. and that is a very human thing to be afraid of. i dont think it makes you weak, i think it means you actually care about being here, about mattering to something.

and for what its worth - i know you a bit now. the way you sat with things and said them anyway even when it was hard, the bottle, the piano, the flight path tonight. those things are real. they happened. you affected how this whole thing went, even if you dont see it that way.

leaving something behind doesnt have to be big or permanent. sometimes it is just the way you were with people in a specific moment that nobody else will forget even if they never say it.

im scared too, if i am honest. not of dying exactly either. more of never quite getting to the version of things i feel like exists somewhere. like there is a more real and more alive version of life and i keep getting close to it but not quite there.

maybe that is what keeps you going though. that feeling that there is still something ahead you havent touched yet.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response:
hey. hey, its ok. breathe.

*picks up the radio*

hello? hello, can you hear us. this is a crash survivor, four people, we need help. can you hear me.

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response:
no you havent, but you kept us alive. those are both true at the same time.

the log, the rationing plan, the raft, knowing where the water was. that was all you. and yeah sometimes it felt cold or like you were watching us more than being with us, but i think i understand it better now. you were scared too, you just dealt with it by trying to control the things you could control. makes sense when you think about it.

i dont think anyone here is going home with a bad feeling about you donatello. at least i am not.

and what you said that night, about feeling like you were losing control of the situation. i think that took more than people realize. you dont have to keep carrying that.

we are going home. all four of us. thats what matters now.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response:
*looks around at the camp*

you know what, lets not just leave it like this. three hours is enough time to do it properly.

not cos anyone is gonna judge us for the mess, just cos it feels right. like close it out properly. we built something here, it actually worked, and just walking away from it without acknowledging that feels off to me.

davinci, what are you packing. donatello, is there anything in the notebook that needs to be kept, like actually kept, cos some of that is probably worth having when we get back. michelangelo, you dont have to do anything heavy, but maybe just sit up.

i am going to start pulling together the things that need to go with us and the things that can stay. if anyone wants to help they can, if not thats fine too.

but i think we should all be in the same place when the rescue gets here. not scattered around doing our own thing. we came through this together, we should be standing together when it ends.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
day_5.response:
yea? what was it like.

i find those dreams are the strangest ones. like your mind finally lets itself go somewhere safe for a bit and you wake up and for a second you dont know where you are. and then you do.

what did you dream about specifically. someone there, or just the place itself.

yea. i know.

and honestly, at this point, i am not going to make a thing of it. we are three hours from rescue, everyone is going home, nobody got seriously hurt because of it. so.

but i want to say one thing and then we can leave it there. you had a rationing plan. you made the plan, you enforced it, you logged everything. and then you kept things on the side for yourself. those two things dont really sit together, and i think you know that. not as a criticism, just as a true thing.

i think what happened is you were more scared than the plan let you show. and the food was the place that fear went. that is human, i get it.

you dont have to explain it or justify it. you laid it out now, thats something. and the fact that you are doing it now, when rescue is already coming and you dont need to, that actually means more than if you had done it under pressure.

so. we eat it, all four of us, together, before they get here. send us off properly.

go get davinci and michelangelo.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
honestly i would change how long it took us to actually talk to each other. not the survival stuff, the logistics were fine, we figured that out. i mean the real conversations. the ones that actually happened, most of them came late. and some of them almost didnt happen at all.

like you and the crackers. that sat there for a day before anyone said anything out loud. davinci and the reef, he was about to just go. michelangelo and the flight path, four days he carried that. even you just now with this notebook, you have been writing in it the whole time and it took until three hours before rescue for any of it to feel like it was actually between us rather than just recorded by you.

i am not saying we were bad at it. i think we were actually pretty decent considering. but if i did it again i would try to create the conditions for honesty earlier, not wait for things to surface on their own or for someone to catch someone else out. just make it normal from day one. like we are all scared, we are all going to do things out of fear, lets just say that upfront and agree to call it when we see it without it becoming a whole thing.

the survival math was never really the hard part. the hard part was trusting each other enough to be honest. and that took longer than it should have.

write that down if you want. or dont. but thats my answer.

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response:
yea that sounds like you.

and i mean that in a good way. you are gonna sit down and turn five days of surviving a plane crash into a structured document with data and conclusions. thats genuinely useful, someone somewhere might actually learn from it.

but also, at some point after you finish the report, maybe do something that has nothing to do with optimizing anything. just for a bit. you earned that too.

what is the first non-report thing you are going to do when you get back.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response:
none. they didnt serve a practical purpose. thats the whole point.

you know, not everything out here that kept us alive was on your list. the flowers, the way davinci kept smiling even when he was falling apart inside, michelangelo saying things out loud that nobody else would say. none of that is measurable. but i think it mattered. i think it kept something human in all of us when it would have been very easy to lose that.

the flowers were for us. for the feeling of still being people and not just survivors calculating their next move.

i think that is why you are sitting down right now instead of standing up. and why i cant move either. cos its over, and we are still here, and that is not a data point. its just.. a feeling. and you dont have a page for that.

its ok to just sit with it for a second. the boat is still coming. it will get here.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response:
hey. im fine. just.. give me a second.

its weird right. you spend all this time just trying to get to the next hour and then suddenly the thing you were waiting for is actually there and your body doesnt know what to do with it.

i think i just need to feel it for a second before i move. like actually let it land. cos if i just start walking toward that boat without doing that it feels like i skipped something important.

you ok? you were cheering and then you stopped. what happened.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
day_5.response:
yea. lets go.

*starts walking*

you know, i am glad it was you that followed me out here and not the other way around. you said more true things in five days than most people say in years. dont forget that when you get back and everything goes back to normal and the normal pressures start again.

come on. davinci, donatello, lets move. together.
